title: Cost input sensitivity and finance sign-off memo
body:
Purpose:

This is an internal review memo capturing the current cost-model input candidates, calibration approach, sensitivity findings, and a checklist for Finance sign-off. Objective is to get alignment on the canonical data sources (billing vs. telemetry), acceptability bands for key coefficients, and any residual conservative cushions Finance requires before we lock assumptions into the pricing rollout.

Context and scope:
- Focus: Hosted API & Dedicated baseline (not Private on-prem packaging).
- Models in scope for this iteration: rwd-v2-13B, rwd-v2-70B, and a generic embedding model.
- Primary outputs: recommended canonical inputs (numbers), sensitivity summary, finance sign-off checklist, and open questions.

Summary of recommended canonical inputs (proposed):
- GPU unit cost per hour (amortized infra): $1.85/hour (derived from committed pricing + expected utilization).
- Effective GPU tokens/sec (end-to-end observed p50): 42 tokens/sec for 13B, 14 tokens/sec for 70B.
- Average token length per request: 220 input + 180 generated = 400 tokens (apply per-route overrides).
- KV cache hit rate (workload avg): 35% (range explored 20%–60%).
- Batch size effective (continuous batching): 1.7 average requests per inference batch.
- Quantization overhead savings: 20% cost reduction on 13B when using int8 profiles, 9% on 70B (empirical from bench runs).
- Networking egress, storage, misc: add $0.002 per request overhead as staging umbrella (tokens->bandwidth).

Primary data sources and provenance:
- Billing records: GCP invoice line items aggregated by project tag (sheet: billing_rollup_2025Q4). Use as the ground truth for $/hour and amortization base. (Linked sheet: billing-rollup link)
- Runtime telemetry: prod-traces + serving-metrics (p50/p95 latencies, tokens/sec) sampled between 2025-09 to 2025-11 (sheet: runtime-samples). This is the main source for tokens/sec, batch sizes, and KV cache hit rates.
- Benchmarks: dedicated microbench runs (bench/quantization-2025-10) measuring kernel improvements, memory pressure, and per-token GPU occupancy for different quant levels.
- Sizing docs: Dedicated capacity plans and expected headroom (sheet: dedicated-sizing-projections) used to compute amortized hourly cost given committed machines.
- Finance working data: historical committed spend and committed discounts (Marissa Holt provided a summary extract).

Calibration approach (how we turned raw data into inputs):
1) Align billing window: map telemetry windows to invoice periods to account for seasonality (we applied a 3-week alignment window and weighted by request volume).
2) Remove outliers: discard top 0.1% long-running rare jobs (not representative of API traffic).
3) Tokens/sec mapping: compute p50 tokens/sec by sampling request traces grouped by model + sequence length buckets; we use p50 as baseline and p95 for tail buffer.
4) Cache impact: cache hit rates estimated from prefix-match logs. We treat cache effect multiplicatively on generated tokens only.
5) Quantization: use bench delta on per-token GPU time (bench median) and map to cost via $/GPU-hour.
6) Batching: continuous batching efficiency measured from queueing traces; effective batch multiplier applied to tokens/sec to reflect concurrency benefits.

Key calibration sensitivities (high-impact assumptions):
- GPU utilization / amortization: +/-10% change yields ~7–9% change in unit cost. Finance wants an explicit 5% conservative buffer if we use committed discounts as basis.
- KV cache hit rate: moving from 35% -> 20% increases per-request cost by ~6% on average for chat-style traffic.
- Effective batch multiplier: using a conservative 1.3 instead of 1.7 increases per-token cost by ~8%.
- Quantization adoption rate: assumed 40% of workload eligible for int8; if actual adoption is 20% cost savings halve.

Sensitivity matrix (high-level):
- Scenario A (base): canonical inputs above => unit cost per 1k tokens: $0.018 (13B).
- Scenario B (pessimistic infra + low cache): +12% cost => $0.0202 per 1k tokens.
- Scenario C (better batching + higher cache): -9% cost => $0.0164 per 1k tokens.
- Notes: these are illustrative; full sensitivity table in linked spreadsheet (sheet: sensitivity-matrix).

Open questions / unresolved items:
- Which GCP committed discounts should be treated as sustainable baseline vs. one-off? (Finance input needed)
- How to roll Private deployments into the same model (we need a separate amortization model for onsite hardware).
- Region-level adjustments: current model uses global blended GPU cost; should we produce per-region variants? (engineering asks for per-region SLO costing).
- Edge-case traffic (large context documents with >16k tokens): do we apply special surcharge bands or cap model selection?
- Customer-level cache behavior: we have limited sample coverage for high-cache users; is it acceptable to use blended cache rate?

Tickets/PRs to resolve before sign-off:
- FIN-342: confirm sustainable committed discount treatment (owner: Marissa Holt).
- OPT-429: finalize sensitivity pivot points and publish to API pricing team (owner: Priya Nair).
- INFRA-778: per-region GPU cost extract (owner: Diego Morales).
- ENG-quant-87: quantization bench anomalies (owner: Evan Chen).

Finance sign-off checklist (items Finance usually requires):
- [ ] Canonical billing extract attached and reconciled to workbook totals (link to billing_rollup_2025Q4).
- [ ] Conservative buffer specified for GPU amortization and committed discounts (proposed buffer: 5%).
- [ ] Documentation of sampling windows and outlier removal methodology (this doc + runtime-samples sheet).
- [ ] Approval on categorization of misc overhead ($0.002/request) and whether to allocate as tokens or per-request fixed fee.
- [ ] Agreement on adoption assumptions for quantization and caching (percentages and rollout timeline).
- [ ] Two finance approvers listed and signed in comments (required for final PR).

Notes to reviewers (how to use this doc):
- Please edit the canonical values in the linked "1xT-optimize-cost-inputs" spreadsheet — this memo should reflect the final cell names.
- If you have alternate calibration logic, leave a comment with the proposed formula and a brief justification.
- Use the sensitivity sheet to run alternative scenarios; include scenario name and rationale when requesting sign-off.

Immediate next steps (owners):
- Diego: extract per-region GPU pricing and add region columns to billing_rollup (due 2026-03-12).
- Evan: re-run quantization bench for 70B under high-memory pressure config and post updated numbers to bench sheet (due 2026-03-09).
- Priya: produce a reconciled version of the sensitivity matrix with p95 tail buffers included (due 2026-03-11).
- Marissa (Finance): confirm sustainable discount policy and add two approvers for sign-off (due 2026-03-13).

Quick decisions requested from Finance:
1) Accept proposed GPU amortization buffer: 5% (yes/no).
2) Treat misc overhead as per-request fixed fee vs. per-token marginal fee (preference needed).
3) Approve base scenario for public pricing pilot (target date 2026-03-20).

Appendix (short notes on methodology):
- We intentionally use p50 for baseline throughput because p95-skewed baselines inflate unit costs and mask optimization potential; p95 is reserved for tail provisioning policy.
- Cache hit measurements are conservative (only count strong prefix matches). We have a tagging plan to improve this measurement fidelity in Q2.
- Batch multiplier accounts for both hardware-level packing and runtime continuous-batching effectiveness; measured by correlating queue depth to tokens/sec over minute windows.

Draft history / edits log:
- 2025-11-03: initial draft (Amara) 
- 2025-11-16: added bench runs and quantization deltas (Evan)
- 2026-01-22: adjusted token length averages after product routing review (Priya)
- 2026-02-28: added finance buffer proposal and sign-off checklist (Marissa)
- 2026-03-05: updated sensitivity numbers after sampling window expansion (Amara)

---

Notes to self: keep memo terse for Finance. They want 1-sentence justification per input and one spreadsheet with reconciled cells. Avoid speculative adoption rates without an explicit rollout plan.
